narrative: This pull covers 25 to 31 Aug against 18 to 24 Aug (a wider gap than the usual day to day read, since the last refresh had fallen behind). Spend rose 31.8% to ₹10,900 (from ₹8,272), and leads grew even faster, up 36.3% to 218 (from 160) — so cost per lead actually improved slightly, down 3.3% to ₹50.00 (from ₹51.70), even as CPM crept up 2.8% to ₹78.67. CTR softened 4.9% to 1.25% and hook rate fell a sharper 12.0% to 26.04% (from 29.59%), so the CPL improvement is coming from volume and mix, not from stronger creative pull.

The spend increase is concentrated in two places: 'VP_Animated-Static_17July26' scaled almost eightfold (₹715 to ₹5,583) while its own CTR barely moved (0.84% to 0.86%), and a brand new ad, 'VP_VastuShanti_25Aug26', launched straight in at ₹2,765 with a strong 2.17% CTR. Two older ads were cut hard — 'VP| Vastu video|NewContent|07Jul26 – Copy' down ₹2,422 and 'VP_VastuShanti_AD_11Aug2026' down ₹1,310 — both of which had climbing CTRs at the smaller spend level (1.33% to 2.09% and CTR flat on the other), a sign the account cut back on some ads that were still performing.

Reading this against the ops funnel needs a caveat: the manually logged sales data only covers 2 of the 7 days in this window (25 and 26 Aug), so a raw total comparison isn't fair. On just those 2 days, contacted to MQL conversion was unusually high (73.4% vs 58.9% over the full prior week) and MQL to SQL held steady (59.6% vs 62.3%), but SQL to Converted looked weak (25.0% vs 54.5%) — on a base of only 28 SQLs and 7 conversions, which is too small to call a real trend.

callout.title: Volume and a strong new ad are carrying CPL, but hook rate is quietly falling as spend concentrates
callout.body: CPL improved this window only because leads outgrew spend, not because creative pull got stronger — hook rate fell 12.0% and CTR fell 4.9% while spend concentrated hard into one ad ('VP_Animated-Static_17July26', now 8x its prior spend) plus one new ad. If hook rate keeps sliding as that ad keeps absorbing budget, expect CPL to reverse upward even with strong lead volume. Separately, the sales funnel read for this window is based on only 2 of 7 days of ops data — the apparent dip in SQL to Converted rate should not be treated as confirmed yet.

actions: Watch 'VP_Animated-Static_17July26' closely: it now carries the largest share of spend in the tab but its CTR hasn't moved, and hook rate tab wide fell 12.0% this window. If its own hook rate is soft, treat further scaling with caution rather than assuming this window's good CPL will hold.
'VP_VastuShanti_25Aug26' launched strong (2.17% CTR, ₹2,765 spent in its first days) — a good candidate for continued scaling alongside, or in place of, the ads that were cut this window.

Follow up with the sales team for the missing 5 days of ops data (27 to 31 Aug) before drawing any conclusion about the SQL to Converted dip seen in the 2 days currently logged — the sample is too small to act on.
CPM's rise (+2.8%) is mild on its own, but paired with softening CTR and hook rate it's worth a routine creative refresh check next pull rather than an emergency one.

narrative: This pull covers 25 to 31 Aug against 18 to 24 Aug. The clearest driver is 'VP_Baby-Shower_CarouselAD_17Aug26', whose CTR more than doubled (1.56% to 3.38%) while it also took on more spend (+₹720, to ₹4,793) — this single ad looks responsible for most of this window's CTR, hook rate, and chat volume gains. 'VP_Garbhsanskar_Testimonial_VideoAD_15Jun26' grew more modestly (+₹749, CTR roughly flat), while 'VP_Garbhsanskar_Testimonial_VideoAD_19-02-26 – Copy' was trimmed slightly (-₹237) with its already-low CTR unchanged.

The ops funnel again only covers 2 of the 7 days in this window (25 and 26 Aug). On those 2 days, contacted to MQL (22.7%) and MQL to SQL (50.0%) rates were close to the prior full week's 21.5% and 45.8%, but zero of the 5 SQLs converted in that short window — on a base this small, that reads as noise rather than a real drop in close rate.

callout.title: A genuine creative win, not a lag or spend effect: chats up 83.6% on only 15.6% more spend
callout.body: Cost per chat falling 37.0% while spend rose only 15.6% is a real efficiency gain, and it lines up cleanly with 'VP_Baby-Shower_CarouselAD_17Aug26' more than doubling its own CTR (1.56% to 3.38%) as it absorbed more budget — this is the clearest single driver of the tab's improvement this window, and also reverses the hook rate decline flagged as a risk in recent reads. The ops funnel read for this window is partial (2 of 7 days), so the 0 conversions logged there should not be read as a new problem.

actions: 'VP_Baby-Shower_CarouselAD_17Aug26' is carrying this window's gains almost single handedly (CTR 1.56% to 3.38%, plus more spend). It's a strong candidate for a further, deliberate budget increase while it's performing this well.

Watch frequency and hook rate together as 'VP_Baby-Shower_CarouselAD_17Aug26' continues to scale — this window's hook rate recovery (+52.3%) is real, but creative fatigue risk rises the longer a single ad carries this much of the spend.

narrative: This pull covers 25 to 31 Aug against 18 to 24 Aug, still on a small, early sample (33 cumulative days with any spend). actions: Static-1's improving CTR (0.40% to 0.64%) suggests it deserves a slightly larger share of the next incremental budget increase relative to Video1.
Cost per chat's rise (+9.3%) is explained almost entirely by CPM's rise (+6.3%); this is a scaling cost, not a red flag, especially with frequency essentially flat.
Continue treating week over week swings on this tab as directional only, given the still small cumulative sample (33 days with spend).
No ops funnel exists for this tab; keep relying on Meta chat volume, CTR, and hook rate as the primary read on performance.

callout.title: A real ROAS decline this time, not the usual attribution lag
callout.body: Umbartha and Vedic Sanskar both carry a known Meta side attribution lag where the most recent 2 to 3 days of purchases look undercounted and self correct the following week. This pull's day level numbers don't show that pattern for Umbartha — Meta purchases (15) and Shopify orders (16) for the window are close, including on 29 to 31 Aug specifically. So this window's ROAS drop (8.65x to 4.66x) reflects a real decline in orders and revenue against higher spend, concentrated in 'VP_Umbartha_VideoAD_14-04-2026 – Copy' softening as it scales, not a reporting artifact.

actions: Hold or trim further scaling on 'VP_Umbartha_VideoAD_14-04-2026 – Copy' until its CTR (down to 2.46% from 2.64%) and conversion stabilize — it's the main driver of this window's higher spend and lower ROAS.

This window's ROAS drop is confirmed real, not a lag artifact (day level Meta and Shopify purchase counts track closely through 31 Aug) — treat it as a genuine signal needing a creative or audience review, not something that will self correct next pull.
'VP_Umbarthakit_18july26' is small but improving (CTR 1.72% to 2.98%); a modest test budget increase here is a reasonable hedge while the primary ad set is under review.
Given the ₹25 lakh a month portfolio goal, hold Umbartha spend roughly flat rather than scaling further until ROAS recovers back toward its recent 7 to 9x range.
